eyebrow: Is it running, and what's it doing right now?
code:
$ systemctl status nginx
● nginx.service - A high performance web server
     Loaded: loaded (/lib/systemd/system/nginx.service; enabled)
     Active: active (running) since Mon 2026-10-05 09:02:11 UTC; 3h ago
   Main PID: 1012 (nginx)
caption: status shows active/inactive state, uptime, and the main PID

code:
$ sudo systemctl restart nginx
$ sudo systemctl stop nginx
$ sudo systemctl start nginx
caption: start/stop/restart affect the system, so all three need sudo

eyebrow: Running now vs. running at every boot

steps.label: systemctl start nginx
steps.sub: runs it right now, no effect on reboot

steps.label: systemctl enable nginx
steps.sub: symlinks it to start at boot, no effect now

steps.label: systemctl enable --now nginx
steps.sub: both — up now and at every future boot

eyebrow: A minimal custom unit for Northbridge's sync worker
code:
[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/node /opt/northbridge/sync-worker.js
Restart=on-failure
User=nbapp

$ sudo systemctl daemon-reload
$ sudo systemctl enable --now nb-sync
caption: Restart=on-failure is why a crashed worker comes back without a page at 3 a.m.

subtitle: Running a job on a schedule, not just once at boot.
